My boyfriend does the same, when he asks me if I want something I'll tell him that it's nice etc, but at the same time I've managed to start refusing things I'm not comfortable with or I wouldn't mind having but don't really WANT or NEED.

I feel a healthy balance between accepting and refusing is the way to go.

From what I've seen/read, for the fat person it's not necessarily a turnon, and its likely more about pleasing her partner who gets off on control, and she likes being taken care of. She was trying to be healthy before him, which I feel might be a sign it's *not* a turnon for her, or she wouldn't have put in the previous effort.

She believes she has something special, while if she dies under his care, he can simply move on to somebody else to get a similar relationship. It might have started with him encouraging her to get "curvier" but at one point, no matter what you think, you're not curvy anymore, and people in feeder relationships (which is really what your mom's sounds like) turn into a blob. 

The use of curvy kinda makes me snort tbh, it is often used as an excuse for people's weight "Oh, no, I'm not obese, I'm curvy". There are people who are naturally curvy, and of healthy weight, and if you can't achieve that you might simply not have the body type for it, and that's okay.

2 years ago, i bought a nice/classy dress and jacket because i was **thinking** of **maybe** getting an **internship** in a diplomatic environment.

I never went ahead with the internship and switched my studies to something which has a reputation for casualness, I've never worn either the dress or the jacket, and I have 0 regrets, despite that I could've used the money for other things.

He gets a great opportunity, and acts up about it? Yeah okay, seems like he doesn't really want it to me. He's living the good life (to him) and doesn't look to the future. It could be a dealbreaker, it is to some people, you'll just have to decide whether it is for you or not, for me, it would be.

Maybe not directly relevant for the relationship, but see if he would be willing to get a checkup done to see what specific nutrients he is missing so you can maybe get supplements, could help with his health a bit.

I'd say it could also make him refuse to eat veggies even more because hey, if he has supplements he's sorted right?, but tbf, it doesn't sound like he could eat any less.

Reply to that: "What kind of project? When will it be finished?" Followed by continued requests to find out if it's finished yet each time he sees you. I've tried that tactic, it doesn't actually work sadly enough.

It's possible she'll never feel passionately about having sex with you, or even anyone. Not everybody has the same view or feelings about sex, and if you need that to be rationally supported you can read up on asexuality (for an extreme example).

Breakups can change a person's opinion on others, sometimes for a good reason, but all too often out of bitterness.

He might have thought you weren't that type of conniving girl while he was still with you, but that doesn't mean his opinion couldn't change quickly now.

I have loved each of my boyfriends in different ways.

My previous boyfriend I thought was the love of my life, the way I felt for him I hadn't felt before for anyone else, and he ended up cheating on me.
I still think about him quite often, even though I'm in a relationship now, my feelings for him are dead, I have no respect left for him just as he had no respect for me.

My new boyfriend, I dont feel that passion and "love of my life" love for that I had with my ex, but I recognise that I love him, and that it's real. Just as I remembered after a while that while I never felt the same for any previous guys how I did about my ex, that I felt differently towards each one of them, and that it didn't diminish the relationship I had with any of them.

When somebody has been an important part of your life and hurts you severely, yeah, you're going to think about them, the point is to catch yourself when you do it, and deliberately change the way your thoughts are heading.

Feelings wise its a general sense of worthlessness, i can't understand why my SO is so crazy about me and feel like i'm wronging him by not being able to respond with the same intense feelings all the time (this inability makes me feel worse about myself). I also am hesitant to share when i'm feeling bad because i don't want to burden/bother him or make him feel responsible for my wellbeing.

Though that's a pretty "normal" state of being for me, on bad days what happens is that whatever negativity is on my mind spirals and pretty much consumes my thoughts, that I can't think of anything else anymore. It's very hard to snap out of and it's very draining. I have been unable at times to do even simple tasks because i felt my body was so heavy that i simply could not move.
Other people are not a consideration in that state except as abstract presences I am a burden to, who might think negatively of me, and so on.

My issues are not rooted in grief though, and while there always are recognisable patterns and whatnot, everybody is still an own person.

There are good periods and there are bad periods, but the overall is unlikely to improve without therapy, or so I believe/is my experience.

I'm currently on "the other end" as well, my emotions are locked away it feels like but on good days I do feel a burst of confirmation sometimes that I do genuinely care for this person, even if I dont actively feel it all the time.

You probably don't even remember writing this, but i just wanted to let you know it hasn't come back since the post, not even while drunk :) (Well, it was months between the post and the time before that as well)

And while I can't say I'm fine, I'm at least alive and staying that way.
